The river is near my tree. It runs along the edge of the wood, just beyond the meadow. I can hear it at night, the water lapping and the fish jumping. I don’t like it much. The water is cold and the fish are slippery. I prefer the dry places where I can sit and listen to the wind.

A stream. It runs through the meadow behind the wood, and it is where I drink and where I hear the water fall in the dark. I can tell the difference between the stream and the river farther away by the sound. The stream is shallow and clear, and the river is deep and loud. I do not like the river. A stream runs past the edge of the wood, just beyond the meadow. I can hear it in the dark, the water slipping over stones and the pebbles jumping in. I do not drink from it, but I watch the owlets drink.

The stream that runs past the meadow. I can hear it all night, the water sliding over stones, the pebbles splashing. It is the only water near my tree. I drink from it when I need to, and I watch the owlets drink from it in the spring.

A stream runs past the edge of the wood, just where the meadow starts. I can hear it at night, the water splashing over stones and the fish leaping. I don't go near it, not even to drink. I prefer the damp earth under my tree.

The stream that runs by the meadow. It is wide and fast, with stones and reeds. I can hear it from my tree, especially when the wind is still. The stream that runs through the meadow behind my oak. It is wide and fast in spring, narrow and slow in winter. I can hear it from my perch, the water slapping against stones and the fish jumping. I do not drink from it, but I watch the herons and the kingfishers come to feed.

Shrews. I catch them in the meadow at dusk. Their scent is the first thing I notice when I turn from the hollow. They are quick and they smell bad, but they are also the most common. I eat them in the dark, the light is too bright.
Most of my diet is voles. They come out at dusk, run across the meadow, and I wait in the ivy. I catch them with my feet, then carry them back to the hollow. One in the morning, two in the evening.

My favourite prey is the pebble. Small, quick, and full of life. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and I wait until the right moment. When I strike, it's fast and silent. Peas. Small, fat, juicy, and slow. They are easy to catch in the meadow at dusk. I eat them in the hollow of the ash.

Shrews. They come out at dusk, scurrying along the lane. I hear them from the hollow, a squeak, a scuttle, a quick burst of wing. I drop and catch them with a thump. I eat the body, leave the skull.
